newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Chase CEO sees no need for U.S. rate rise now.
newsitem.headline: Chase CEO sees no need for U.S. rate rise now.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp chairman and chief executive Walter Shipley said on Monday the Federal Reserve should continue to hold off from raising interest rates again so long as inflation looked under control.

In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Shipley said the Fed's action in raising rates by 25 basis points on March 25 and holding off from another rise since then had been a good approach that had kept markets guessing.
"I would expect that the economy would continue to perform about where it is. Inflation will continue to be difficult to find," said Shipley, who was attending the International Monetary Conference.
He said the Fed should continue to watch out for signs of inflation, but not "try to anticipate something that might not be there".

He said historical indicators might suggest worrisome inflation growth was likely at this time, but this was not actually happening because increased global competitiveness and productivity had changed the inflationary threat.
